question: Which state of India records the highest reserves of lignite coal as reflected in the data of 2014 from the Mines and Minerals Yearbook?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Tamil Nadu has the highest reserves of lignite coal in India, accounting for approximately **80% of the country's total reserves** as per the 2014 data from the Mines and Minerals Yearbook.
 
• The Neyveli Lignite Corporation (NLC) in Tamil Nadu is the leading organization for lignite mining and thermal power production in the region.
 
• Major lignite reserves in Tamil Nadu are located in the **Neyveli** and **Jayamkondam** areas.
 
• Lignite coal is primarily used in **thermal power generation** and as a fuel in industrial applications.
 
• Tamil Nadu's lignite mining and power generation activities contribute significantly to the state's **energy sector** and economic development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lignite Coal:**

 
 
• Lignite, also known as brown coal, is a lower grade of coal with a high moisture content and lower calorific value compared to bituminous and anthracite coals.
 
• It is primarily used as a fuel for generating electricity in thermal power plants.
 
 
 
• **Neyveli Lignite Corporation (NLC):**
 
 
• NLC is a public sector enterprise under the Ministry of Coal, responsible for lignite mining and power generation in Tamil Nadu.
 
• It operates several thermal power plants and is a major contributor to India's electricity grid.
 
 
 
• **Other States with Lignite Reserves:**
 
 
• While Tamil Nadu has the largest reserves, other states like Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Jammu & Kashmir also have significant lignite deposits.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Concerns:**
 
 
• Lignite mining and usage contribute to environmental challenges, including deforestation, air pollution, and greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• Efforts are being made to adopt cleaner technologies and reduce environmental impact.
 
 
 
• **India's Coal Classification:**
 
 
• India classifies its coal reserves into four types: anthracite, bituminous, sub-bituminous, and lignite, with lignite being the youngest and least carbon-rich form.
 
• Lignite reserves are primarily found in the southern and western parts of the country.
